Here are simplified definitions for the technical terms found in the text:

**Nanotechnology**
This is the science of working with extremely tiny things. It involves building or changing materials one atom or molecule at a time. By doing this, scientists can create new materials that have special abilities or properties that you wouldn't find in larger versions of the same material.

**Atomic scale**
This refers to the size of atoms, which are the basic building blocks of all matter. It is incredibly small—so small that you cannot see atoms with a regular microscope.

**Molecular scale**
This refers to the size of molecules, which are groups of atoms bonded together. Molecules are slightly larger than individual atoms but are still microscopic.

**Supramolecular scale**
This refers to structures formed when multiple molecules stick together or interact with each other. It is a level of organization just above individual molecules, involving how these molecules group and arrange themselves.

**Matter**
This is anything that takes up space and has mass. In everyday terms, it is the "stuff" that makes up everything you can touch, see, or interact with in the physical world.

**Novel properties and functions**
"Novel" means new or unique. In this context, it means that the materials created through nanotechnology have special new features or abilities that they didn't have before, or that larger versions of the material do not have.
